subject: Canary config: request for auto-fallback & version pin during rollout
raw_thread:
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@nimblepay.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: NimblePay SRE <sre@nimblepay.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 16:23:00 -0700
Subject: Canary: request for autorevert thresholds + temporary version pin

Hi Laura,

Quick note from the SRE side at NimblePay — during our initial A/B rollout of the payments-instrument model (v2027-08-a) we saw an increased p99 tail and a handful of timeouts on peak. We haven't crossed your contracted uptime SLA yet, but given the nature of payment flows we need an explicit safety net: automatic fallback to the previous stable variant (v2027-07-stable) and a temporary version pin for 48 hours if fallback triggers.

Attached is a short PDF with the telemetry snapshots and a dash link. Can Redwood authorize a runtime policy that:
- Immediately switches traffic back to the pinned stable variant when the canary p99 > 700ms for 3 consecutive 5-min windows OR error rate > 1% sustained for 10 minutes.
- Pins the stable variant for 48 hours after fallback (no automatic re-roll unless explicitly approved by NimblePay).
- Provides SRE-level visibility into warmup status and KV-cache hit rate during the pinned period.

We want to avoid manual escalations at 2am — this is a safety automation ask. Please let me know what you need from our side (additional telemetry, SLOs, or an exec approval path).

Thanks,
Olivia
Director, Platform Reliability
NimblePay

-----

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@nimblepay.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Canary: request for autorevert thresholds + temporary version pin

Thanks Olivia — appreciate the heads-up and the PDF. We can do that; below is a proposed minimal-safe config that balances your availability concerns with operational stability on our side. If you approve, I'll route this through our on-call and change-control for an immediate runtime policy deployment.

Proposed runtime policy (summary):
- Trigger conditions (any):
  * canary_p99 > 700ms for 15 minutes (3× 5-min windows)
  * OR canary_error_rate > 1.0% for 10 minutes
  * OR tail_timeout_count > 5 in 10 minutes
- Automatic action:
  * immediate traffic reroute to v2027-07-stable (100% of requests)
  * mark v2027-08-a as quarantined and stop new rollout jobs
- Post-fallback controls:
  * automatic pin on v2027-07-stable for 48 hours
  * telemetry retention: full per-token traces for 48h for filtered sample of payment flows
  * require a manual 'replay & vet' signoff from NimblePay SRE + Redwood eng before re-enabling canary
- Additional safeguards (recommended):
  * warmup step triggered on failover: sequential cache-warm requests before ramping live traffic if cold cache detected
  * circuit-breaker: GPU util > 92% for 5 minutes will trigger an alert (not automatic fallback unless accompanied by latency degradation)

Questions for NimblePay:
1) Are the trigger thresholds above acceptable?
2) Is 48 hours enough or do you want 72?
3) Confirm the on-call SRE to notify for manual vet (name + pager).

I'll loop in Rishi and Karthik to confirm the runtime rollout mechanics and any impact to SLAs/documentation.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference

-----

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 19:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Canary: request for autorevert thresholds + temporary version pin

+1 to Laura's plan. A few engineering clarifications and additions from the runtime side:
- Implementation detail: autorevert will be enacted by route-policy layer; this can be pushed as a hot config and is reversible. We'll record the event in the deployment audit log (ID + timestamp).
- Add a secondary trigger: sustained increase in queue_length > baseline + 4× stddev for 10m. This catches request backpressure that sometimes precedes p99 jumps.
- For pinning: we'll surface a 'pinned_until' timestamp in the model metadata and block subsequent automated rollouts. Ops note: we need a handoff playbook so Redwood on-call can coordinate post-fallback remediation with NimblePay SREs.

I'll prepare the runtime change (hot config) as soon as NimblePay confirms thresholds. If approved, we can apply the policy with a 30-minute observation window and an explicit rollback path.

Rishi
Sr. Product Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 08:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Canary: request for autorevert thresholds + temporary version pin

Adding engineering acceptance criteria to make sure the switch doesn't cause collateral issues:
- Warmup plan: preflight 50 synthetic payment requests against v2027-07-stable to populate KV cache before cutover; monitor cache_hit_rate target >= 80% within 10 minutes.
- Telemetry sampling: keep full traces on 5% of payment requests for 48h post-fallback (anonymized tokens), plus aggregated latency histograms at 1-min resolution.
- Resource guard: if GPU mem pressure > 88% or model-serving queue growth is > 3× baseline, we will block re-roll until SRE signoff.

If NimblePay is OK, I'll schedule the hot config rollout and post with the audit log id. We should also add a short note to the SLA appendix indicating that automatic fallbacks are catalogued as operational mitigations and don't reset uptime windows unless there is a confirmed platform fault.

Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
